thread.title: The True Potential Of A NEO Smart Economy - NEO USD (Cryptocurrency:NEO-USD)

author: Vishesh Raisinghani
title: The True Potential Of A NEO Smart Economy - NEO USD (Cryptocurrency:NEO-USD)
text:
Consider buying a house. Across the world, the process of purchasing real estate is somewhat similar. You hire an agent who shows you properties, negotiates with the owner, the owner arranges for paperwork for the property, you pay the broker commission, you prepare all the paperwork to get a mortgage, you sign the deed, and finally get the keys.
It’s a long and arduous process that can sometimes take months and cost thousands of dollars. All this in a world where you can buy a similar amount of Apple ( AAPL ) shares for free and within seconds on your Robinhood app. Real estate transactions are just one of many sectors where bureaucracy, middlemen, lack of structure, and convoluted rules are creating friction for ordinary buyers and sellers.
It’s precisely this sort of inefficiency experts hope blockchain technology might be able to weed out in the near future. The often overhyped technology that powers the world’s most well-known cryptocurrency, Bitcoin (BTC), may never achieve most of the outlandish things people think it is capable of, but it can already has a track-record of immutability, low costs, high security, and decentralization. All these factors can eliminate middlemen and eradicate the need for fragmented silos of paperwork.
In the crypto developer’s cyberpunk dream of the near future, everyone’s identity is stored on a public blockchain and connected with their crypto assets. A person can simply use their private key to buy a cup of coffee or purchase a plot of land in another country with a single click on their smartphone. Smart contracts, or pieces of software that execute automatically on a blockchain, can be used to register employment contracts, real estate transactions, medical histories and educational backgrounds.
Some have started to call this smart contract-driven future a ‘smart economy’. Market research suggests this space could experience compounded annual growth of over 32% for the next five years, breaching $300 million in market value by 2023.
Going by this traditional estimate, smart contract platforms have immense potential for growth beyond 2023. However, picking a winner in this volatile and nascent market is easier said than done. There’s no reason to believe the ETH will continue to dominate the smart platform market. Cardano, Lisk, Tron, EOS, and Stellar (XLM) all offer unique advantages and different frameworks for developers trying to build decentralized applications on a blockchain. But the one I find most interesting is NEO ( NEO-USD ).
A NEO Way
Source: Medium
NEO, formerly known as AntShares, was launched a year before Ethereum in 2014. Founded by Da Hongfei and Erik Zhang, the blockchain-based platform allows developers to build scalable decentralized applications (or dApps).
The team’s primary ambition is to create the blockchain-driven, smart contract-based smart economy I described above. So far, the project’s core strengths are the size of its developer community and the technical advantages of the NEO blockchain over rival platforms like Ethereum and Cardano.
NEO’s developer base is one of the most active and committed communities in the crypto space. Over the past four years the project has managed to gather over 1K contributors and over half a million community members. Most of these developers and users are expected to congregate in Seattle next month for the NEO developer conference .
While NEO has a sizable developer community, the crowd lags behind other similar platforms on the basis of activity. Over the past twelve months, NEO developers have made 168 commits to Github , far behind rivals like Cardano (3,683), Stellar (678), and Ethereum (1,213). More commits indicates faster development.
One possible explanation for this discrepancy in developer activity could be the fact that most NEO users and developers are Chinese. NEO’s founding team, initial documentation and online community were overwhelmingly Chinese. China’s Great Firewall has targeted GitHub on and off for the past decade.
However, the NEO developer community has become more globa l in recent years. City of Zion, the largest NEO developer community is location independent and spread across the world. Other developer collectives like NeoResearch, Key Makers, and NEO St Petersburg Competence Center (NSPCC) are based in Latin America, Japan, and Russia respectively. This growing global developer base should have a clear impact on the blockchain’s progress in the near future.
Regardless of visible activity, the NEO dev team has managed to create a serious threat to Ethereum’s market dominance. The transaction throughput on the NEO network is orders of magnitude higher than ETH. The NEO blockchain can handle over 2,000 transactions per second, compared to Ethereum’s meager 15 per second.
That’s not the only advantage NEO offers over its bigger, more popular rival. The blockchain consensus mechanism is based on what’s known as the delegated Byzantine Fault Tolerant (dBFT) , which is a modified version of proof-of-stake ( POS ). Ethereum is also trying to adopt its own version of PoS, however the timeline for that transition is vague , at best.
Developers trying to commit to the Ethereum network need to learn a whole new language called Solidity, while NEO devs can simply apply C# and Java, Python and Go. This is a critical advantage that should help the NEO team attract more devs in the near future.
The fact that a new developer can simply start coding and committing to the NEO blockchain without any hurdles is a clear indication that NEO is more viable for mass adoption than Ethereum. Easier programming has helped companies like Apple ( AAPL ) and Google ( GOOG ) build their core developer base in the past decade, and this is likely to play out in crypto as well.
Another clever aspect of the network’s infrastructure is NeoQS (Quantum Safe) , a complex mechanism that should protect the NEO blockchain from the onslaught of future quantum computers. As far as I can tell, NEO is one of the few blockchain projects taking the threat of quantum computing seriously.
All things considered, NEO is a serious contender as a base layer for the smart economy of the future. At $560 million, NEO’s market cap is just a fraction of the potential market size of the smart economy within the next decade.
